summary: Buffered single-byte stream output used by the printf-family engine: decrements the remaining-buffer count a2[1]; when the count goes negative the byte is handed to the low-level writer sub_58CF35(a1, a2), otherwise it is stored at *a2 and the write pointer advances. If the emit result is -1 (error sentinel) the running count *a3 is set to -1, otherwise it is incremented. Returns the count pointer a3.

operations.description: Decrement the remaining-buffer count a2[1] and test its sign; a negative value indicates the current buffer is exhausted.
When the buffer is exhausted, emit byte a1 through the underlying writer sub_58CF35(a1, a2) and capture its return value.
Otherwise store a1 at the current write pointer (*a2) and advance the pointer (*a2)++.
Branch on whether the emit result is -1: set *a3 = -1 on error, else increment the running count (*a3)++.
Return a3, the stream byte-count pointer.
